sections.description:
Short title extent and commencement

PRESIDENT'S (POST﷓PROCLAMATION) ORDER NO
PRESIDENT'S (POST‑PROCLAMATION) ORDER NO. 17
of 1977
PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(DISQUALIFICATION FOR MEMBERSHIP ORDER, 1977
1. Short title,
extent and commencement.‑‑(1) This Order may be called the
Parliament and Provincial Assemblies (Disqualification for Membership) Order,
1977.
(2) It extends to the whole of
Pakistan.
(3) It ,hall come into force at
once.

sections.shortTitle: Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Disqualification for Membership Order 1977
sections.description:
Definitions

PRESIDENT'S (POST﷓PROCLAMATION) ORDER NO
PRESIDENT'S (POST‑PROCLAMATION) ORDER NO. 17
of 1977
PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(DISQUALIFICATION FOR MEMBERSHIP ORDER, 1977
2. Definitions.‑In
this Order, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,‑
(a) "misconduct"
refers to conduct after December 1970, and includes bribery, corruption,
jobbery, favouritism, nepotism, wilful maladministration wilful misapplication
or diversion of public moneys or moneys collected, whether by public
subscription or otherwise, and arty other abuse of whatsoever kind of power or
position, and any attempt at, or abetment of, such misconduct;
(b) "respondent" means the person in
respect of whom a reference is made under clause (2) of Article 4; and
(c) "Special Court" means a Special Court
established under Article 3.

Establishment of Special Courts

PRESIDENT'S (POST﷓PROCLAMATION) ORDER NO
PRESIDENT'S (POST‑PROCLAMATION) ORDER NO. 17

3.
Establishment of Special Courts.‑(I) The President may, by notifica tion
in the official Gazette, establish once or more Special Courts for the purposes
of this Order.
(2) Each Special Court shall consist of a person who
is a Judge of a High Court.
(3) A Special Court shall sit at such place as the
President nay, by notification in the official Gazette, specify in this behalf.

sections.shortTitle: Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Disqualification for Membership Order 1977
sections.description:
Cases to be enquired into and decided by special Court

PRESIDENT'S (POST﷓PROCLAMATION) ORDER NO
PRESIDENT'S (POST‑PROCLAMATION) ORDER NO. 17
of 1977
PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(DISQUALIFICATION FOR MEMBERSHIP ORDER, 1977
4. Cases to be enquired into and decided by Special Court.‑(1) A Special
Court shall enquire into and decide cases relating to the misconduct of a
person who is holding, or has held,‑‑
(a) under the Provisional Constitution Order or the
Interim Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, the office of
President or Governor, or
(b) under the Interim Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan or the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, the office of Prime Minister, member of
the President's Council of Ministers, Federal Minister, of State, Attorney‑General,
Chief :'Minister, member of a Governor's Council of Ministers, Provincial
Minister, Parliamentary Secretary, Advocate General or member of the National
Assembly or of the Senate or of a or of a Provincial Assembly.
(2) The Special Court shall not proceed to enquire
into any charge of misconduct except on a reference in writing made to it.
(a) in the case of a person who is holding, or has
held, the office of Preside, Prim Minister, member of the President's Council
of Ministers Federal Minister, Minister of State. Attorney‑General,
Federal Parliamentary Secretary, member of the National Assembly or of tie
Senate, Governor, Chief Minister, member of a Governor's Council of Minister,
or Provincial Minister, by the President; and
(b) in the case of a person who is holding, or has
held, the office of Provincial Parliamentary Secretary, Advocate‑General,
or a member of a Provincial Assembly other than the Chief Minister or a member
of a Governor's Council of Ministers or a Provincial Minister, by the President
or, if the President so requires, by the Governor.
(3) On receiving a reference under clause (2), the
Special Court shall scrutinize the necessary records relating to the charge
mentioned in the reference, and‑
(a) it, as
a result of such scrutiny, it is of the opinion that no charge can be established,
return the reference to the authority making it together with its opinion
thereon; and
(b) in other cases, Issue notice to the respondent
requiring him to show cause why it should not further proceed against him under
this Order.
(4) Nothing in paragraph (a) of clause (3) shall bar any subsequent reference to the Special
Court, except in so far as it relates to a charge in respect of which an
opinion has previously been given by the Special Court under that paragraph.

sections.shortTitle: Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Disqualification for Membership Order 1977

Enquiry by special Court

PRESIDENT'S (POST﷓PROCLAMATION) ORDER NO
PRESIDENT'S (POST‑PROCLAMATION) ORDER NO. 17
of 1977
PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(DISQUALIFICATION FOR MEMBERSHIP ORDER, 1977
5. Enquiry by
Special Court, etc.‑In a case in which the Special Court has issued
to the respondent a notice under paragraph (b)
of clause (3) of Article 4, the Special Court shall, after such further
scrutiny of records and such enquiry as it thinks fit and after giving the
respondent an opportunity of being heard, record its findings and, in case the
respondent is found guilty, he shall stand disqualified for a period of seven
years from being elected or chosen as a member of Parliament or of a Provincial
Assembly.

sections.shortTitle: Parliament and Provincial Assemblies Disqualification for Membership Order 1977
sections.description:
Powers and procedure of special Court

PRESIDENT'S (POST﷓PROCLAMATION) ORDER NO
PRESIDENT'S (POST‑PROCLAMATION) ORDER NO. 17
of 1977
PARLIAMENT AND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLIES
(DISQUALIFICATION FOR MEMBERSHIP ORDER, 1977
6. Powers and
procedure of Special Court.‑(1) A Special Court shall have the powers
of a civil Court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V
of 1908), in respect of the following matters, namely :‑
(a) summoning
and enforcing the attendance of any person and examining him on oath;
(8) requiring the discovery and
production of any document;
(c) receiving evidence on
affidavits;
(d) issuing commissions for the examination of
witnesses or documents; and
(e) requisitioning any public record or copy thereof
from any Court or office.
(2) A Special Court shall have power to require any
person, subject to any privilege which may be claimed by that person under any
law, to furnish such information as in the opinion of the Special Court may be
of assistance to it in carrying out an enquiry under this Order.
(3) The proceedings before a
Special Court shall be deemed to be judicial proceedings for the purposes of
the provisions of Chapter XI of the Pakistan Penal Code (Act XLV of 1860).
(4) Notwithstanding anything
contained in any other law for the time
being in force, a Special Court shall have power to conduit its Proceedings
and regulate its procedure in all respects as it deems fit including, in
particular, the power to refuse to examine any witness or summon any document;
(5) The proceedings before a
Special Court shall be open to the public, unless otherwise directed by the
Special Court.
(6) A Special
Court shall have the powers of a High Court to punish its own contempt.

7. Appeal.‑Any
person aggrieved by a finding of a Special Court under Article 5 may,
within thirty days of the decision of the Special Court, prefer an appeal to
the Supreme Court.

9. Order not to derogate from other laws.‑The provisions of this Order shall be in
addition to and not in derogation of any other law for tire time being in force
and nothing in this Order shall prevent or prejudice the trial or punishment of
any person under any other such law.

10. Saving.‑No proceeding under this Order
against any person who holds or has held an office mentioned in Article 4 for
anything which has been in good faith done or intended to be done in pursuance
of or in exercise of owners vested, or in good faith believed to be vested, in
him at the material time by virtue of that office.
